Surjectivity of either incidence projection rules out a conormal with only one nonzero component. Checked all nine steps with current incidence, implicit/Morse/stationary-phase and packet suppliers. The punctured conormal parameterization has the signed equations T^T p=0 and xi=D^T p. Injective d pi_L gives a local embedded data image. The conormal one-form vanishes and its tangent is Lagrangian by a dimension calculation, so injective left projection implies surjective right differential and an analytic local section. T injective gives invertible fiber Hessian B+i T^T T. In the Schur-complement calculation the imaginary reduced quadratic form is |T Re tau+Dh|^2+|T Im tau|^2; equality would give a nonzero left-kernel tangent, excluded by hypothesis. Thus positivity is strict in every real object direction. The critical value is -q.p and derivative -Xi; adding q.p normalizes the object test phase without changing modulus. The analytic leading coefficient is nonzero and the normalized contour remainder becomes absolute exponential on real parameters, with fixed-derivative errors controlled before distributional pairing. The Gaussian-regularized packet resolution has mass tending to 1. Reader F7-to-F6 relabeling is metadata, with no mathematical change; raw source equals reader-post hash. Checked all six steps and exact local suppliers, including Sjostrand Lemma 2.7/Theorem 2.8 proof (printed pp.15-18) against the local stronger positive quadratic margin. Morse coordinates give a graph with slope below one, enabling Stokes deformation with exponential boundary loss. Cauchy Taylor remainder through degree 2N-1 integrates to C^(N+1) N! lambda^(-N-n/2); the separately bounded full-polynomial tail has the same factorial bound for every N, not an unjustified uniform exponential tail. Gaussian moments yield all coefficients with c0=a(0) on the chosen branch. N=floor(epsilon lambda) is used only for sufficiently large lambda; normalization removes any need for Im Phi0>=0.
